commit.message:
Close share-class and duplicate-assessment review gaps

- Bind the share-class receipt to every written capital cell and value,
  so any later numeric write makes it stale.
- Duplicate or unexpected checker assessments never drive a table re-copy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Show repeated human totals and keep comparison views readable

- Derive every calculated total on a compared statement from the human
  file's inputs, so a total repeated on a sheet (one mTool cell) no
  longer shows blank.
- Stacked worksheet navigation scrolls away instead of covering figures.
- Empty spacer columns no longer make a note table "wide"; human table
  cells keep figures and headings whole.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix agent-trace audit findings from runs 183-185

- Issued Capital lists every disclosed share class before finishing; a
  missing or stale list leaves the sheet flagged on every successful exit.
- Appearance checker reviews tables one at a time, must quote the row it
  faults, and never re-copies on rejected or content-defect evidence.
- Continued-table refusals name the pages and recorded preparation doubt;
  emphasis the formatter cannot remove is reported as a source issue.
- Cross-sheet write hint follows current/non-current; a successful write
  to the suggested cell clears the earlier rejection.
- Mandatory-field feedback offers the audited not-disclosed path, and a
  notes tie-out failure no longer suppresses figures triage.
- Cleanup rejections list every unsafe removal with its location.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Render note emphasis as semibold everywhere notes appear

Bold marks in notes used the browser default "bolder", so emphasis inside
headings and table headers compounded and looked heavier than headings.
The mTool/Copy decorator now stamps un-styled <strong>/<b> with semibold
600, inheriting an already-bold ancestor's weight (any case, !important
tolerated) and leaving explicit source/user weights intact. The editor
CSS mirrors this and uses the prepared-output Arial face and cell size.
Design system documents the rule.

commit.message:
Bind table claims to cited cells and count zoomed pages as inspected

A positive table relationship could cite one real heading and still be
approved while claiming amounts absent from the candidate HTML. Each
relationship must now cite at least one label or heading cell (unless its
table has no text cells) and every figure its candidate_relationship names
must appear in its own cited cells. Contract version bumps to 17 so pages
approved under the looser rule are not reused.

zoom_pdf_region now records the page as inspected, so a missing-policy
report can cite pages the agent read through a zoom.

Addresses Greptile review on #31.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Tolerate spacing and look-alike characters in table cell evidence

The table verifier compared the model's quoted cell text exactly against
the whitespace-collapsed manifest text, so a stray space or curly quote
marked a correct table unverified and triggered needless repair rounds.
Both sides are now normalised (NFKC, whitespace, quote/dash look-alikes)
before comparison; citing a different cell still fails.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Fix bounded completion and source-verification failure handling

Hand formatter events to the queue safely and show zoom steps

Greptile review:
- view_pdf_pages is synchronous, so its activity callback ran on a worker
  thread and called put_nowait on the server's asyncio.Queue directly.
  queue_event_sink now hands each event to the queue's loop with
  call_soon_threadsafe.
- zoom_pdf_region had no activity wording, so its steps were dropped live
  and in History. It now reads "Zooming into source page N (region)".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Compare page transcripts by the pages they returned

Greptile review: the supersede check used requested pages. read_page_text
returns at most ten pages, so a later request for 1-14 (returning 1-10)
removed an earlier 5-14 transcript and lost pages 11-14. Parsing request
args also crashed compaction when a rejected call carried pages=5.

Read returned pages from the "=== Page N" markers in each result instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Show notes-formatter sub-agents in Activity

Notes formatting runs one agent per sheet, or per table group on large
sheets, but Activity showed one flat list of identical stage messages.
Each formatter pass now reports its own steps, like the Sheet-12 notes
sub-agents.

- notes/formatter_activity.py records started/working/finished-or-failed
  status and tool calls (reported by the tools, so model requests keep
  their non-streaming transport). Events stream live under agent_id
  "notes-formatting" and are saved on the pass's run_agents row with the
  time each event happened.
- A pass cancelled at its deadline is recorded as a time-limit failure;
  an earlier cancellation stays "stopped".
- The live Notes formatting tab and History show sub-agent tabs; the
  combined view names each sub-agent on its lines. Runs saved before this
  change keep the existing view.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Stop page transcripts displacing each other during compaction

Run 179 (Nielsen SOFP) read 217 pages across 26 distinct pages and hit its
step limit. Text compaction kept only the newest read_page_text result per
tool name, so reading one page batch replaced the previous batch with a
placeholder and the agent re-read both in a loop.

- Page transcripts are compacted only after a later read covers all their
  pages; the placeholder names the pages.
- The soft watermark now measures the current request size (latest model
  response usage), not the running total of re-sent tokens, which passed
  the old 60,000 default by the third request of every healthy SOFP run.
  Default raised to 100,000 (healthy SOFP requests peak at 49k-67k).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Address Greptile review: shared revert snapshot, visible save warning, exact line map

- Give the first formatting pass and the post-re-copy pass one shared start
  time, so the second pass no longer deletes the first pass's revert snapshot.
- A failed save of a corrected table to the prepared document is now a
  warning in the result summary instead of being silently dropped.
- The line map reports one entry per contiguous grid-column run of the same
  stroke kind, with its grid span, so side-by-side single and double lines and
  partial lines under merged cells are described accurately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep person ownership, serialize source corrections, and preserve partial re-copy results

- Re-check human ownership inside the formatter's final write transaction,
  so a person saving identical HTML mid-pass keeps the note.
- Hold a per-document lock across the prepared-document correction
  read-modify-write so simultaneous corrections both survive on disk.
- A provider failure during table re-copy or the follow-up formatting pass
  now stays on the affected row instead of discarding saved rows, counts,
  and verification receipts.
- Remove trailing whitespace flagged by diff check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Style only a table's leading heading rows as headings

Preparation uses <th> for any cell that labels a row or column; the display
treated every <th> as a column heading and made it bold. A row label beside
data cells (VTech note 19) or a total captured as heading cells (note 71)
therefore showed bold that the source does not have, and no agent could
remove it. Heading styling now applies only to thead rows or all-th rows
before the first data row; a lower <th> renders as a data cell. Same rule in
the decorator (review, Copy, mTool) and the editor (tableAlign.ts + CSS).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Let one page re-copy correct every table with the same defect

Live VTech page 24: the re-copy correctly fixed the named total row and the
identical defect in the second table on that page, and was refused for
changing 'outside the named table'. Text outside tables still may not
change; every changed table must keep its words and figures and pass the
shape check, and a second table is saved only if it is independently
eligible. Re-copy usage is recorded even when refused. The verifier is told
that graphical rules are the formatter's job, as the capture prompt already
says; full verification is still required.

Live: note 71 re-copied in 16 s (both tables), rebuilt note matches its
source, formatting and visual check pass on all three tables.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Replay recorded page-banner removals when rebuilding a re-copied note

Live VTech run: the notes needing a re-copy had page banners removed by the
cleanup stage, so they matched their source only through the cleanup
receipt and were refused. Removals address short text blocks, never tables,
so they are replayed onto the rebuilt note and the receipt is rewritten onto
the new render. Refusal reasons for several tables in one note are kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Re-copy wrongly copied tables from the PDF instead of flagging them

A table copied wrongly from the PDF (VTech note 71: a total captured as
heading cells) could only be flagged: the formatter may not change table
structure, and notes must match their frozen source blocks.

- Preparation flags an all-heading-cell row holding amounts below the data.
- The visual reviewer labels findings style or structure; structure is never
  a pass and skips the style correction round.
- notes/table_recopy.py maps a structural finding to one source table and
  re-copies it with preparation's own capture and verification prompts.
  Gates: nothing else on the page changes, same words and figures, a real
  structural change, shape check clean, independent verification.
- The source block and every cell built from it are corrected in one
  transaction, so notes still equal the render of their blocks; history in
  notes_source_block_revisions (schema v52). Edited cells, cells that no
  longer equal their source, continued tables and blocks used on another
  sheet are refused and stay flagged.
- The prepared document on disk is updated so a rerun keeps the fix.
- Rebuilt notes get one ordinary formatting pass and visual check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix layout line placement found in live runs; add boxed tables

Live A/B on runs 348/349 showed three defects:
- Lines were placed by locating cells with Tag equality, which compares
  content, so equal amounts ("2,077,740" in four columns) all resolved to
  the first cell. Locate by identity.
- Lines had to meet whole cells on both sides, rejecting a common shape: an
  amount underline above a full-width section row. A line now needs whole
  cells on one side, which carries it; it still cannot cross a rowspan.
- A missing one-line format_summary discarded every layout; it is optional
  and listed before notes.
Boxed text tables with vertical dividers had no description; add
frame: grid.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Formatter describes table structure; code compiles it into formatting

The formatter used to write per-cell styling operations while code guessed
which cells were amounts from their text in five places. Unusual tables
broke whichever guess was weakest, and the AI mis-addressed cells.

- The formatter returns a SheetLayout: per table, one role per grid column
  (label/amount/date/text), optional row roles (bold, indent, shaded) and
  lines (after_row, from_col, to_col, single/double).
- notes/table_layout.py validates each note against its live tables
  (table count, grid width, bounds, overlapping lines, lines that would cut
  a merged cell or cross a rowspan) and compiles it into patch operations,
  starting with a reset of formatter-owned cell properties.
- A visual correction compiles onto the pass's original HTML, so it fully
  replaces the first layout; bold stays additive.
- The reviewer keeps every evidence input and gets the layout as context.
- Editor saves record style_source="human"; the formatter never overwrites
  those notes, even on retry. content_origin cannot identify a person
  because the notes reviewer AI also stamps human_modified.
- Fallback alignment: a full-width merged first cell stays left (Python
  decorator and tableAlign.ts).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Harden notes formatting against misread rules and false review failures

Runs 347-349 failed visual review mainly on rule position (one shared
edge read as two rules), single-rule thickness, right-aligned year labels
and a theme grid the prompts assumed but the house style does not have.

- Add notes/rule_map.py: one entry per physical horizontal line, resolved
  by the border-collapse winner and named by the row it sits below. The
  formatter and visual reviewer read it instead of raw border CSS.
- Single-rule thickness is no longer reproduced or judged.
- Formatter and reviewer receive the resolved appearance (house default
  borderless, no fill) and the preparation tier.
- numeric_cells skips the description column.
- Preparation flags a lone header ending in a currency/unit caption as a
  misplaced amount-column heading, so the existing repair loop fixes it.
- Formatter cannot remove bold/italic; revert-snapshot pass comparison
  uses full timestamp precision.

Live A/B on run 348 notes (same model): first-check flags 14 -> 4 of 29
tables; one legitimate unresolved note in both.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Quieter technical detail, aligned setup headings, fewer status repeats

Technical detail rows match the plain activity list: small dots,
regular text, plain timings, single dividers above each row, no boxes or
pills, and provider Markdown shown as words. The workstream detail uses

chevron after the title and a summary only when folded; format dots and

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Activity divider, diagnostics in the header, top-aligned note numbers

Saved Activity gets the same full-height Grey 100 divider as the live run
and Notes, and drops the Run activity heading that repeated the tab.

its privacy note becomes hover text. Source-note numbers in the Notes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add writing and microcopy rules to the design system

New Writing and microcopy section: labels, options, titles and buttons
carry the meaning; helper text only for formats and limits, non-obvious

from this app; and a hidden-helper test, also added to the UI review

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Hide the top bar on main pages; simplify filing setup and confirmation

Main pages have no top bar; sub-pages keep one back link and Log out
moves beside the account in the sidebar. Filing setup is one row of four
segmented choices, reporting periods included. Commentary sentences are
removed, the detected unit is a small badge, and once preparation is

summaries unless something needs a decision. Note templates use plain
names and setup disclosures put their chevron on the left.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

One top-bar treatment: back links on sub-pages, no repeated titles

The top bar showed a back link on Settings but a grey label repeating
the page title elsewhere. It now carries one back link, in one style, on

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Match the Figures worksheet divider to the Source PDF divider

The PDF column's resize handle draws a one-pixel Grey 100 rule; the
